Module: Note (GAP-QB-01): TrainerQuestionAIService.generatePayload computes `categoryId`/`difficultyId` local fallback variables (defaulting to 1L/14L when the request doesn't provide them) but never actually uses them — buildSystemPrompt(mode, quantity) doesn't take them as parameters, and buildUserInput(req) reads req.getCategoryId()/req.getDifficultyId() directly (the raw, possibly-null request fields), not the computed fallback locals. Net effect: when a Trainer omits categoryId/difficultyId when asking the AI to generate a question, the prompt sent to Gemini literally says "CATEGORY_ID(DEFAULT): null" instead of a real default — the intended fallback behavior is dead code. Looks like an unfinished feature, not deliberate. Not fixed this round; test asserts the actual (gap) behavior per code-first principle. Re-verified 2026-07-24, still reproduces.

Note (GAP-QB-02, new 2026-07-24): TrainerQuestionServiceImpl.getQuestionDetail and .updateQuestionBankGroup (isGroup=true branch) derive ownership entirely from the group's child Questions via `!questions.isEmpty() && !questions.get(0).getCreatedBy().getId().equals(user.getId())`. When a QuestionGroup exists but currently has zero linked Question rows, `!questions.isEmpty()` short-circuits to false and the ownership check is skipped entirely — any authenticated trainer can view (getQuestionDetail) or overwrite the passage text and inject new questions into (updateQuestionBankGroup) another trainer's empty group without being its owner. Likely an unintentional oversight (ownership should probably be stored on QuestionGroup itself rather than derived from its children). Not fixed this round; tests assert current (buggy) behavior per code-first principle.
